cards.headline: LiquidAI's d1-3B beats bigger models on Decision Index
cards.hook: Small model, big score. LiquidAI claims the top spot.
cards.tldr: LiquidAI released open-weight decision models d1-3B and d1-omni-600M today. The d1-3B scores 48.57 on the Decision Index 0.2.1, beating larger competitors. This availability allows immediate local testing for edge applications.
cards.memeLine: Big models are out. Small decisions are in.

cards.headline: EmbeddingGemma 2: On-device embeddings for the rest of us
cards.hook: A lightweight multimodal model that fits in your pocket's RAM.
cards.tldr: Google has released EmbeddingGemma 2, a 740 million parameter model built on the Gemma 4 architecture. It is licensed under Apache 2.0, allowing commercial use without restriction. The key selling point is efficiency: with quantization, it requires only ~191MB of active RAM for text-only weights on a Google Pixel 11 Pro. This makes it suitable for local file retrieval tasks directly on mobile devices. When paired with the larger Gemma 4 model for reasoning, it creates a hybrid workflow. This reduces cloud dependency and latency for specific embedding needs.
cards.memeLine: Your phone just got smarter about files.

cards.headline: The Quiet Burden of Bot Traffic on Wikipedia
cards.hook: AI agents are consuming resources, leaving humans to clean up.
cards.tldr: Recent reports indicate that a significant majority of heavy traffic on Wikimedia projects originates from automated sources. This surge has forced volunteer editors and security teams to spend considerable effort detecting and reversing unwanted changes. The infrastructure strain is measurable, with bandwidth usage increasing substantially in recent years due to this activity. It is a logistical challenge rather than a dramatic takeover, requiring steady maintenance to keep the platform functional for human readers and writers.
cards.memeLine: We built an encyclopedia; now we build the broom.

cards.headline: Trump’s Super Intelligence Force Is a Rebrand, Not a Breakthrough
cards.hook: The new agency has the name but lacks the actual superintelligence.
cards.tldr: The administration is launching the Super Intelligence Force, led by officials like Jay Clayton and Andrew Ferguson. This initiative uses terminology from AI research to describe a government body that does not possess Artificial Superintelligence. While ASI refers to self-improving systems surpassing human intellect, this new force is an administrative structure. The move highlights a gap between technical reality and political branding. It serves as a signal of intent rather than a deployment of advanced technology. Watch how this rebranding affects future policy discussions on AI governance.
cards.memeLine: Super Intelligence Force: Now with 100% less actual superintelligence.

cards.headline: OpenAI Safety Chief Quits, Citing Broken Culture
cards.hook: Geoffrey Irving leaves OpenAI after warning AI could kill us all by the end of the decade.
cards.tldr: The departure of a key safety figure at OpenAI highlights internal friction over model release protocols. Geoffrey Irving has joined warnings from Anthropic regarding existential risks. The company recently paused a next-generation model due to researcher concerns. This sequence suggests that safety checks are becoming a bottleneck for development rather than a seamless integration. The industry is watching to see if these pauses will become standard or remain exceptions.
cards.memeLine: Culture is broken, but the compute keeps running.
